dataset.description: The user studies conducted in task T2.2 will aim to investigate the influence of avatar and environment features on the perception of inappropriate behaviour in 1 to N virtual social interactions. Its objective is to identify and characterise the key factors that modulate how users perceive inappropriate behaviour. The task will delve into various avatar characteristics (e.g., realism, movement, animation, gender, ethnicity, attraction, intimidation, voice, and age) and virtual environment aspects (e.g., size, population density, social setting, and context) while exploring different evaluation methods. Assessment will encompass subjective responses (questionnaires), physiological measures (e.g., eye-tracking, GSR) and behavioural responses, including their impact on proxemics (e.g., stop distance, analysis of the walking trajectory).

format: The experimental studies will produce and use primary (calculated and experimental) data. The primary data includes responses to questionnaires (CSV, XML), performance (CSV, XML), observations (Word, Excel, pdf), images (jpg, tiff, png) and videos (avi, mp4, m4v, mpg).

dataset.preservation_statement: If the dataset is relevant for the research community, it will be freely available either through the associated paper submission (e.g., supplemental materials) or in a dedicated open repository (e.g., zenodo)

security_and_privacy.description: Data will be stored in computers with an encrypted hard drive and require user credentials for logging in.

dataset.title: Study No4 Impact of Avatar and Environment Characteristics on Perception of Inappropriate Behaviour

dataset.description:
This study focuses on understanding the conditions in which active and efficient bystander behaviour can emerge (size of the group, type of users), and whether tools developed in META-TOO can facilitate it. There will be a series of experiments where the Metaverse users will be a bystander of inappropriate behaviour and their reactions will be analysed, including who, when, and how reacted. Behavioural indicators will be followed by short online questionnaires and semi-structured interviews.

The first study, currently being conducted, uses the Golden Rule Embodiment Paradigm (Banakou & Slater, 2021) to investigate whether participants who experienced harassment during a job interview (compared to those who had a respectful interview) will increase the likelihood of intervening in another harassment situation.

format: CSV, Plain Text files, Audio files

dataset.title: Study No1 Bystander behaviour in the Metaverse

dataset.description:
We will conduct a series of experimental scenarios carried out on a simulation of popular metaverse platforms with a diverse population of users. Questionnaires, the number of reported incidents, and a qualitative analysis based on semi-structured interviews will be used to verify the training’s effects.
Participants will go through a simulation of a user training led by an intelligent (AI-controlled) virtual human. The participant will embody 3 avatars which represent people who may suffer from racism, queerphobia, or fatphobia.
dataset.preservation_statement: It will be published as a supplementary material to a research publication.
